text: The effect of the major metabolite of aspirin, namely salicylic acid, upon the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) of normal and G6PD-deficient red cells has been studied. Salicylic acid was shown to inhibit this pathway in proportion to the amount present. However, at any concentration of this substance, there was less inhibition of the PPP in G6PD-deficient than in normal red cells.
